subject: It is not just a book
preview: 66 books, over 40 authors, 1,500 years, and somehow one story.

blocks.text: Most of us have held a Bible without ever asking what it actually is.
It sits on a shelf. Or in an app on your phone.
It looks like one book.
But the Bible is not just a book. It is a library.
📚 Sixty six books
✍️ Written by over forty authors
🌍 In three languages, across three continents
🕰️ Over roughly 1,500 years
Empires rose and fell while it was being written. Languages shifted. Cultures changed.
Think about who wrote it.
A king. A shepherd. A fisherman. A tax collector. A physician. A man who used to persecute Christians.
Different backgrounds. Different personalities.
And yet the central message never changed.
Here is what I want you to understand.
The Bible is one story. Not about people reaching up to God, but about God reaching down to us.
Genesis plants the seed. Micah names Bethlehem. Psalm 22 paints the crucifixion before crucifixion existed.
A tree in Genesis. A cross in the Gospels. A tree of life again in Revelation.
That is not random. That is design.
And once you understand how the Bible is put together, a lot of the confusion starts to fade.
In the full article I walk through the Old and New Testaments, the seven kinds of writing inside the Bible, and the people God used to write it.
It is a good one to read before the new year, or to share with someone who is curious about the Bible for the first time.
